displayName: UniBasic (Rocket UniData / UniVerse) → Java 21 · Spring Boot 3
description: Feasibility POC for a real prospective engagement (equipment-finance system, 50-year-old system, business logic in UniData/UniBasic, migrate to Java 17+/PostgreSQL). UniData is the MultiValue database PLATFORM (from Rocket Software); UniBasic is the procedural language that runs INSIDE it — comparable to 'PL/SQL inside Oracle', except UniBasic is a full general-purpose BASIC (drives terminal screens and batch jobs too, not just stored procedures). Calibrated against six real, public UniBasic/Pick-BASIC source files (github.com/zelenko/pick — a UniVerse-backed Eclipse ERP customization; UniVerse is Rocket's sibling MultiValue database, whose BASIC dialect is near-identical to UniData's — a documented, minor dialect delta this schema flags rather than papers over). The claim taxonomy centers on the one thing that has no relational/OO equivalent: a MultiValue 'attribute' can itself hold multiple values and sub-values (field-mark/value-mark/sub-value-mark delimited), addressed with angle-bracket syntax (x<2>, x<1,3>) — every such usage needs an explicit List/nested-list/record shape decision on the Java side, the same category of problem this platform already solved for ABL temp-tables and PHP arrays, but more pervasive here since MultiValue IS the storage model, not an occasional structure. IMPORTANT — no source-execution equivalence: Rocket's only free UniData tier was a 2-user 'Personal Edition' of a since-superseded major version (dev/demo-only, not a scriptable CI runtime), and Rocket's own 'Rocket MV BASIC' tooling is a VS Code editing/debugging extension that talks to a live licensed server, not a standalone interpreter. Verification rests on golden-dataset extraction scoring plus compile+test of the generated Java — exactly the same honest gate structure already shipped for OpenEdge ABL.

claimKinds.label: Invariant
claimKinds.description: Behavioural invariants the routine must preserve across all valid inputs — the business rules a reviewer signs off on and the Java target must uphold.

claimKinds.label: MultiValue dynamic-array usage
claimKinds.description: Angle-bracket multivalue addressing (x<N> = value N, x<N,M> = sub-value M of value N), MATPARSE (split a delimited string into a dynamic array), LOCATE ... SETTING ... (find a value's position, or the ELSE branch when absent), INSERT/DELETE at a located position, DCOUNT (count values/sub-values), and CONVERT a TO b IN x (re-delimiting between value-mark, field-mark, and arbitrary-character representations of the same multivalue string — observed in the real calibration corpus swapping VM for @FM so LOCATE/INSERT could operate on it, then back before writing). Each needs an explicit Java shape decision: List<T>, a nested List<List<T>>, or a fixed-shape record — and the CONVERT round-trip becomes free/implicit once the data lives in a real collection.

fields.name: expression
fields.doc: The MultiValue expression, e.g. 'BR<J>' or 'CONVERT VM TO @FM IN BR'.

claimKinds.label: Numbered field-position access
claimKinds.description: READV/WRITEV (and record-level READ/WRITE combined with a numeric subscript) address a record's attribute by BARE NUMBER (e.g. 'READV WRITER FROM OQ,ID,9' — field 9, no name). This is a real, pervasive fragility in MultiValue business code: the semantic meaning of 'field 9' lives only in the database's DICT (data dictionary) definitions or in institutional memory — NOT recoverable from the source file alone. Every occurrence is captured as-numbered and flagged as needing the client's actual DICT export to resolve to a named Java property; do not invent a business name for a bare field number.

fields.name: file_or_table
fields.doc: The open file/table handle this position is read from, e.g. 'OQ' (opened from ORDER.QUEUE).

claimKinds.label: Record / file access semantics
claimKinds.description: OPEN 'FILE' TO HANDLE ELSE ... (hashed MultiValue file open with an ELSE-clause guard, structurally identical to a not-found guard in other languages), the FIND/READNEXT SELECT-list cursor pattern (EXECUTE a SELECT, then LOOP / READNEXT id ELSE EXIT / REPEAT), versus OPENSEQ/WRITESEQ/CLOSESEQ (genuine sequential OS-file I/O, e.g. a flat CSV/TSV export — a DIFFERENT access model from the hashed-file READV/WRITEV world and must not be conflated with it). The hashed-file cursor pattern maps to a Spring Data query returning a List/Stream; sequential file I/O maps to plain Java I/O or a batch export job.

claimKinds.label: Dynamic / indirect call target
claimKinds.description: CALL @variable(...) (the call target is held in a variable, resolved at runtime — observed in the real calibration corpus as e.g. 'SUBRI = "DICT.PRD.SALES"; CALL @SUBRI(...)') and SUBR('name', args...) (a function-call-style invocation of another cataloged program that returns a value). Both are real inter-program call mechanisms with NO static target in the @variable case — captured as-written (the variable name, or the literal SUBR target), flagged as needing either dataflow analysis or a Java Strategy/registry-lookup pattern rather than a direct method call.

fields.name: target_as_written
fields.doc: The literal token after CALL/SUBR, e.g. '@SUBRI' or 'VZ.GET.VALUE'.

claimKinds.label: Dynamically-built query execution
claimKinds.description: A TCL SELECT ... WITH ... command built via string concatenation, then run via EXECUTE (observed in the real calibration corpus building the WHERE-equivalent by string-concatenating field values directly into the command text). This is dynamic-SQL-shaped: a real injection-risk-equivalent pattern in the source that a Java target must NOT reproduce literally — it should become a parameterized Spring Data query / JPA Criteria query instead. Flag the built command's filter conditions as the invariant to preserve, not the string-concatenation mechanism itself.

fields.name: command_template
fields.doc: The SELECT/filter shape being built, e.g. 'SELECT ORDER.QUEUE WITH STAT = "O" AND ORDER.DATE = <today>'.

fields.name: java_equivalent
fields.doc: e.g. 'a parameterized Spring Data @Query / JPA Criteria predicate'.

claimKinds.label: Side effect
claimKinds.description: Externally-visible state mutations: WRITE/WRITEV/WRITESEQ (record or field write), DELETE, SEND.MESSAGE (inter-user notification via the MultiValue 'Phantom'/messaging subsystem — no direct Java web-app equivalent, needs an explicit notification-port adapter, the same treatment as ABL's SEND.MESSAGE or PHP's mail()), and sequential-file create/append.

claimKinds.label: Edge case
claimKinds.description: Boundary/semantic conditions specific to UniBasic → Java: OCONV/ICONV inline format-mask conversion (e.g. 'RESULT/100"MR2"' — a rounding/scaling mask applied as part of an expression, observed in the real calibration corpus) needing an explicit BigDecimal rounding-mode decision; a missing record leaving a read variable as an empty string via the ELSE branch (not a null — the guard IS the null-check, must not be dropped); GOSUB-paragraph code appearing AFTER a RETURN statement that is genuinely unreachable in execution (observed once in the real calibration corpus) — flag as dead code to confirm with the SME, not to silently port.

claimKinds.label: Open question
claimKinds.description: Ambiguities needing SME/client resolution: the DICT (data-dictionary) definitions needed to name every numbered field position; GOSUB-paragraph → Java method extraction granularity (one method per paragraph, or inline); record-locking semantics (READU/LOCK/RELEASE) — not exercised by this small public calibration sample, a documented gap the real client engagement must validate against actual UniData source; whether this specific shop's '!' comment-prefix convention (seen throughout the calibration corpus, both for commented-out code and a trailing check-in stamp) is universal to this dialect or a local convention; and whether terminal-screen (FORM/paging) logic co-located in the same program needs separate re-platforming (same posture as ABL's FRAME/DISPLAY UI carve-out).

topLevelFields.name: enclosing_type
topLevelFields.doc: The cataloged program/routine name (from the filename convention, per unibasic_parser's design — SUBROUTINE headers carry no name of their own).

ioFieldShape.directionDescription: UniBasic SUBROUTINE parameters carry no IN/OUT keyword — direction is inferred from usage (read-only vs written-to before RETURN) and must be stated explicitly, since the source alone doesn't declare it.

promptHints.emphasis: Every angle-bracket <N> / <N,M> multivalue access, MATPARSE, LOCATE, INSERT/DELETE-at-position, DCOUNT, and CONVERT-mark-conversion is a dynamicArrayUsage claim — resolve the Java shape (List/nested-list/record). Every READV/WRITEV by bare number is a fieldPositionAccess claim — capture the number, do NOT invent a business name for it. Every OPEN...ELSE, SELECT/READNEXT/REPEAT cursor loop, and OPENSEQ/WRITESEQ is a recordAccessSemantics claim — distinguish hashed-file from sequential-file access. Every CALL @var(...) or SUBR('name',...) is a dynamicCallTarget claim — flag static-resolvability honestly. Every EXECUTE of a built SELECT string is a dynamicQueryExecution claim. OCONV/ICONV inline masks, ELSE-branch empty-string-not-null reads, and any code after a RETURN are edgeCase claims. DICT field-name resolution, record-locking (unexercised in this corpus), and the shop's own comment conventions are openQuestions.

calibratedAgainst: Public UniVerse/UniBasic source: github.com/zelenko/pick (Eclipse ERP customization) — 6 real files
Prospective client: equipment-finance ILS system (UniData, 50-year-old, terminal + web front end)
